[LSER.8.3.2] In v1, `persist: <dur>` has **one** semantics for every
backing: it forwards each absorbed sample into the samples plane
([LSTO]). On restart, hydration
re-asserts those samples on the normal assert path ([LSER.9.2.3]) and
the backing — running stats, deque, or signal backing —
**rebuilds deterministically** by re-absorbing them in fact order. v1
does not checkpoint internal structure state, so rehydration does not
depend on any checkpoint cadence and reproduces the original state
exactly (given the pinned backing algorithms of [RDSC.5a]).
